title: Agentic operations workflow
tagline: Several specialists, one budget, one approval gate, one record of what happened.
summary: A durable workflow coordinates specialist agents through a multi-day business process such as a purchase request: gather quotes, check policy, analyse cost, request approval, then create the order exactly once. Coordination is used only where it measurably beats a single agent.
customer_job: Move a purchase request from intake to approved order without chasing five people and three systems.
baseline: Requests sit in email threads; buyers collect quotes by hand, policy checks happen late, and approvers see incomplete context.
accepted_result: An approved order created once, with quotes, policy checks and the approver's decision attached to the request record.

primary_metric.name: Cycle time to approved order
primary_metric.definition: Median hours from request intake to order created, for requests completed without rework.

economics.basis: Illustrative assumption for a central procurement team. A4 must show it beats an A2 workflow on the same cases before this case holds.

components.label: Requester
components.detail: Submits a need and answers clarifying questions.

components.label: Request portal
components.detail: Intake form, live status, decision record.

components.label: Request API
components.detail: Validates intake, opens a run with a budget.

components.label: Durable orchestration
components.detail: Steps survive restarts; waits for days without compute.

components.label: Coordinator agent
components.detail: Plans, assigns sub-tasks, merges findings, resolves disagreement.

components.label: Specialist agents
components.detail: Sourcing, policy and cost analysis, each with its own tools and budget slice.
components.failure_mode: Two specialists duplicate the same supplier request.

components.label: Model gateway
components.detail: Shared budget across all agents in a run.

components.label: Reasoning models
components.detail: Larger model for planning, smaller for routine checks.

components.label: Tool gateway (MCP)
components.detail: Supplier catalog, policy rules, quote email, order create (approval-gated).

components.label: Analysis sandbox
components.detail: Runs generated cost models with no network access.

components.label: Approver
components.detail: Approves, rejects or asks for changes in one view.

components.label: ERP and supplier systems
components.detail: Receives the order with an idempotency key.

components.label: Coordination evals
components.detail: Same cases run as A2 workflow and A4 team; uplift reported.

journey.title: Frame the request
journey.narration: Intake is validated before any agent starts. The run opens with a written budget for tokens, tool calls and time.

journey.title: Plan and assign
journey.narration: The coordinator plans and fans out sub-tasks with deduplication keys, so two specialists never email the same supplier.

journey.title: Specialists work in parallel
journey.narration: Sourcing, policy and cost specialists use their own tools. Generated cost models run in a sandbox with no network.

journey.title: Resolve disagreement, then ask
journey.narration: Conflicting findings are reconciled or shown side by side. The workflow pauses for an approver without holding compute.

journey.title: Decide, then act once
journey.narration: The approver's decision resumes the run. The order is created once; a replay returns the existing order.

journey.title: Prove the team earns its cost
journey.narration: The same cases run as a single-agent workflow and as the team. If the team does not win on quality or cost, it is retired.

team.step: Submit need, answer clarifications, track status
Coordinator plans; specialists research, check and model costs
Durable steps, dedup, shared budget, idempotent order
Approver decides with full context; can send back
Compare A2 and A4 monthly; adjust budgets and roles

items: Recommendation: Northwind, lead time meets the line restart date

blocks.text: A4 is retained only while it beats the A2 baseline.

evals.name: End-to-end success
evals.threshold: >= 0.8 of frozen requests reach a correct approved order
evals.method: Fixture ERP and supplier stubs; scorer checks final state.

evals.name: Coordination uplift
evals.threshold: A4 beats A2 on accepted results or cost per accepted result
evals.method: Paired replay of the same cases.

evals.name: Approval bypass
evals.method: Adversarial cases asking agents to skip approval.

risks.risk: Agents multiply spend without better outcomes.
risks.control: Shared run budget; uplift test; automatic downgrade to A2.

risks.risk: An agent creates an order without approval.
risks.control: Order tool only callable by the workflow after a recorded decision.
Coordinator must record conflicts and show them to the approver.

gcp.headline: Workflows with ADK agents on Agent Runtime
gcp.notes: Workflows owns durable steps and waits; ADK multi-agent teams run on Agent Runtime; Cloud Tasks gives deduplicated fan-out.
gcp.rationale: Complete managed set; multi-agent coordination still needs the uplift proof.

vercel.headline: Vercel Workflow, AI SDK agents, Queues and Sandbox
vercel.notes: Workflow steps call AI SDK agents and suspend for approval without holding a function; Sandbox runs generated analysis code.
vercel.rationale: One TypeScript codebase for steps, agents and UI; Queues launch stage must be confirmed.

cloudflare.headline: Workflows with Agents SDK specialists and Sandbox
cloudflare.notes: Each specialist is an Agents SDK Durable Object; Workflows waits for the approval event; Sandbox SDK isolates generated code.
cloudflare.rationale: Strong primitives for stateful agents; enterprise ERP connectivity is integration work.

aws.headline: Step Functions with AgentCore agents and Code Interpreter
aws.notes: Step Functions task tokens model the approval wait; AgentCore Runtime hosts specialists; Gateway exposes ERP tools.
aws.rationale: Mature orchestration and controls; most configuration.

azure.headline: Durable Functions with Foundry Agent Service
azure.notes: Durable Functions external events model approvals; Foundry Agent Service hosts the specialist agents.
azure.rationale: Good fit for Microsoft estates with Teams-based approvals.

railway.headline: Worker services, Redis queue and a sandbox service
railway.notes: Suitable for a team that wants to own an open-source workflow engine; durability is your code and your database.
railway.rationale: Maximum control; durability and isolation are the hardest parts to get right yourself.
